commitResults.messageTitle: Share homework parser prefixes and messages
commitResults.messageBody:
HomeworkAddCommandParser and HomeworkMarksCommandParser each define the
same "Missing required prefix(es): ... Usage: ..." template with their
own usage text appended, and HomeworkEditCommandParser repeats the
prefix list of HomeworkAddCommandParser.

Copies like these drift apart when one of them is edited.

Let's add the template to Messages next to the similar
MESSAGE_INVALID_FORMAT_WITH_USAGE and fill in each command's usage, and
let the edit parser use the add parser's prefix list. Every message
stays the same.

StudentAddParser has a third variant with a space instead of a line
break; it belongs to another feature, so it is left alone.

commitResults.messageTitle: Build limit messages from their constants
commitResults.messageBody:
Several homework messages repeat a limit that is also a constant: the
365-day and 7-day limits of homework upcoming (in its parser and in the
help window), the 100-character title limit, and the largest mark
2147483647. DueDate also checks `year < 1` with a bare number although
its upper limit is the constant MAX_YEAR.

A limit changed in one place would leave the old number in the
message.

Let's build each message from its constant (Integer.MAX_VALUE for the
largest mark) and add MIN_YEAR. Title.MAX_LENGTH becomes public so that
it can be declared before the message that uses it. Every message keeps
its exact text.

commitResults.messageTitle: Share index lookup across homework commands
commitResults.messageBody:
The add, list, edit, marks and delete homework commands each repeat the
same check that the student index is within the displayed list, and
edit, marks and delete also repeat the checks that the student has
homework and that the homework index is within its list.

Five copies of the same checks can drift apart, for example in the
order of the checks or in the message reported.

Let's move the checks into two methods of a new package-private class,
HomeworkCommandUtil: getDisplayedStudent and getHomework. Each command
still passes its own "no homework" message, so every message and the
order of the checks stay the same. HomeworkStatusCommand has the same
checks but belongs to another feature, so it is left alone.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add a way to copy homework with a new score
commitResults.messageBody:
HomeworkMarksCommand rebuilds the scored homework by passing every
field of the old homework to the five-argument constructor. A field
added to Homework later would have to be remembered there too, or it
would be lost when marks are recorded.

Let's add Homework#withScore next to the existing withStatus, which
copies all other fields, and use it in the marks command.

commitResults.messageTitle: Move homework edit success message to own method
commitResults.messageBody:
HomeworkEditCommand#editHomework looks up the homework, validates the
edit, builds the new homework list, and also assembles a three-part
success message, so it mixes high-level steps with string building.

Let's move the message building into a new private method,
buildSuccessMessage, so that editHomework reads as a list of steps.
The message is unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add hashCode to homework commands
commitResults.messageBody:
The add, list, upcoming, edit, marks and delete homework commands
override equals but not hashCode, so two equal commands can have
different hash codes, which breaks the equals/hashCode contract.

Let's add hashCode over the same fields that equals compares, and
assert equal hash codes in each equals test. Index overrides equals
but not hashCode, so the hash uses the zero-based index value instead
of the Index object.

HomeworkStatusCommand has the same gap but belongs to another feature,
so it is left alone.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add homework defensive checks and assertions
commitResults.messageBody:
HomeworkUpcomingCommand accepts a negative number of days, which gives
a window that ends before it starts. The homework code also has no
assertions, although StrictArgumentTokenizer#extractValue relies on an
invariant that its caller sets up: a quoted value starts and ends with
a quote.

Let's reject negative days in the constructor after the null check,
assert the invariant, and test the negative-days and null-date
constructor arguments that have no test yet.

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep displayed students when upcoming list fails
commitResults.messageBody:
homework upcoming shows the full roster before it builds its result, so
if an unexpected error stops the command, the tutor sees the internal
error message and has also lost their search, filter or sort.

A failed command should leave the display as it was, like the other
homework commands do.

Let's build the result first and show the full roster only after that
succeeds. A successful command still shows the full roster, so every
"Student N" in the result matches the student list.

commitResults.messageTitle: Make the upcoming homework list easier to read
commitResults.messageBody:
HomeworkUpcomingCommand pairs each homework with its student's roster
position in a Map.Entry, so the code reads getKey() and getValue()
instead of names that say what they hold. It also repeats the
singular/plural choice of "record" from HomeworkListCommand, and turns
the zero-based position into a one-based number differently from that
command.

Let's use a private DueHomework record for the pair, add
HomeworkListCommand#getRecordWord for both commands, and add 1 to the
position as homework list does. The output is unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Move save-failure rollback to its own method
commitResults.messageBody:
LogicManager#execute parses and runs the command, decides whether to
save, saves, and on a failed save also restores the data, the student
filter and the display order step by step. The restore steps are at a
lower level of abstraction than the rest of the method.

Let's move the three restore steps and their comment into a new
private method, restoreModel, so that execute reads as a list of
steps. The behavior is unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Check save-failure rollback and logic arguments
commitResults.messageBody:
LogicManager undoes a command whose changes could not be saved, but
nothing checks that the data and the displayed students really match
what they were before the command. Its constructor also accepts null
arguments, which fail later with a less helpful error.

Let's assert that restoreModel restored the data and the displayed
students in their order, and reject null arguments in the constructor
with requireAllNonNull, with a test for each null argument.

commitResults.messageTitle: Share field parsing between storage adapters
commitResults.messageBody:
JsonAdaptedHomework and JsonAdaptedStudent each have an identical
toModelValue method that parses a required JSON field, and they differ
only in the message for a missing field.

Let's keep one body in JsonAdaptedHomework that takes the message
format as a parameter, and let each adapter's toModelValue pass its own
format to it. The call sites and every message stay the same.

commitResults.messageTitle: Move homework checks out of student conversion
commitResults.messageBody:
JsonAdaptedStudent#toModelType converts six student fields, then
converts and validates every homework entry inline, then does the same
for lessons, so its homework loop is at a lower level of abstraction
than the field conversions around it.

Let's move the homework loop into a new private method,
toModelHomeworks, next to toModelSubjects. The checks, their order and
their messages are unchanged. The lesson loop belongs to another
feature, so it is left alone.

commitResults.messageTitle: Move roster duplicate check to its own method
commitResults.messageBody:
StudentRoster#setStudents looks for two students with the same
identity in a nested loop inside the method that replaces the roster,
so the check is three levels deep and mixed with the replacement.

Let's move the loop into a new private method, hasDuplicateIdentity,
so that setStudents reads as copy, check, replace. The behavior is
unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Include lessons in student null checks and docs
commitResults.messageBody:
Student gained a lesson list after its homework constructors and
withHomeworks were written, but their Javadoc still describes only the
six profile fields and the homework. The main constructor checks every
argument for null except the lessons, and the AddressBook copy
constructor's Javadoc lacks its final period.

Let's say what happens to the lessons in each Javadoc, add lessons to
the requireAllNonNull call, and add the period.

commitResults.messageTitle: Name the file attribute views in file utility
commitResults.messageBody:
FileUtil#copyPermissions checks the supported file attribute views
with the bare strings "posix" and "acl".

Let's name them ATTRIBUTE_VIEW_POSIX and ATTRIBUTE_VIEW_ACL, so that
the checks say what the strings are.

commitResults.messageTitle: Remove repeated setup in saving tests
commitResults.messageBody:
Seven LogicManagerTest tests build their expected model with
`new ModelManager(getTypicalAddressBook(), new UserPrefs())`, which
TypicalStudents#getModelWithTypicalStudents already provides, and four
tests format the same expected save error message. Four tests with a
storage that always fails also assert that the data file does not
exist, which can never fail because that storage never writes.

Let's use getModelWithTypicalStudents, add a DUMMY_IO_ERROR_MESSAGE
constant, and remove the four assertions that cannot fail.

commitResults.messageTitle: Share the failing model in homework command tests
commitResults.messageBody:
The add, edit, marks and delete homework command tests each build the
same anonymous ModelManager whose setStudent throws, to check how the
command reports an internal error. The upcoming command test builds
its own failing model twice.

Let's add TypicalStudents#getModelFailingOnSetStudent for the four
tests, and a private helper for the two upcoming tests.

commitResults.messageTitle: Check displayed students in command failure tests
commitResults.messageBody:
CommandTestUtil#assertCommandFailure checks that a failed command
leaves the address book unchanged, but not that it leaves the
displayed students and their order unchanged. A command that reset a
search, filter or sort before failing would still pass.

Let's also assert that the displayed students are the same, in the
same order, after the failure. Every existing test still passes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test homework commands on a filtered student list
commitResults.messageBody:
The homework command tests run every command on the full student list,
so no test checks that STUDENT_INDEX refers to the displayed list after
a search or filter, or that an index beyond the displayed list is
rejected although the student exists in the roster.

Let's add both cases for add, list, edit, marks and delete, with the
third student in the roster shown as the only displayed student.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test homework commands on completed homework
commitResults.messageBody:
Every homework in the edit, marks, list and upcoming command tests is
ASSIGNED, so no test checks that editing or scoring completed homework
keeps it completed, or that both lists show the COMPLETED status.

Let's add a COMPLETED_MECHANICS fixture to TypicalHomeworks and one
completed-homework test for each of the four commands.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test largest indices, roster nulls and hash codes
commitResults.messageBody:
Some partitions of homework and saving code have no test:
HomeworkDeleteCommandParser is not tested with the largest int indices,
which the other homework parsers already accept in their tests;
StudentRoster#setStudent with a null argument and setStudents with a
null student are untested at the roster level; and
AddressBook#hashCode never runs in any test.

Let's add a test for each, and assert that two equal address books
have equal hash codes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Tighten storage tests
commitResults.messageBody:
Three storage tests are weaker or harder to read than they need to be:

* Two JsonAddressBookStorageTest names end in
  `_throwDataLoadingException`, unlike the `_throwsX` form of the
  other tests.
* A JsonAdaptedStudentTest test checks only that two homework records
  load, not which ones.
* Two JsonAdaptedHomeworkTest helpers build the homework JSON by hand
  with the title, subject and due date written out again.

Let's rename the two tests, assert the exact homework list, and build
the JSON in a toJson helper from the VALID_* constants.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test help window focus and key handling
commitResults.messageBody:
MainWindow moves keyboard focus back to the command box when the help
window closes, so the next command can be typed at once, but no test
covers it. HelpWindowTest also does not check that a key other than
Esc, Page Up or Page Down leaves the help window as it is.

Let's add a MainWindowTest test that moves focus to the result
display, closes help with Esc and checks that the command box has
focus again, and a HelpWindowTest test for another key. The new focus
test fails if the focus handler is removed.

commitResults.messageTitle: Correct homework and saving docs
commitResults.messageBody:
A few statements in the guides no longer match the app:

* The UG intro to homework upcoming mentions only the score, but each
  line also shows the completion status.
* DG "Saving after a command" says the save-failure message always
  comes from Command#getSaveFailureMessage, but a
  DataFileConflictException keeps its own message, and the list of
  commands that override that method leaves out EditCommand and
  HomeworkStatusCommand.
* The DG says a read-only data file is reported before anything is
  written, but the folder and the .lock file are created first.

Let's correct each statement, and name LogicManager#restoreModel in
the rollback step.

commitResults.messageTitle: DG: Add activity diagram for saving after commands
commitResults.messageBody:
DG "Saving after a command" describes in four numbered steps when
LogicManager saves and how it undoes a command whose changes cannot be
saved, but has no diagram, so the two decisions are hard to see at a
glance.

Let's add a small activity diagram of these steps above them.

commitResults.messageTitle: Explain leading zeroes in rejected homework marks
commitResults.messageBody:
A score such as 05/10 is rejected with the general score message,
which lists only whole numbers, a positive total and the range of the
marks. Both 05 and 10 seem to meet those rules, so the message does
not tell the user what to fix, although the User Guide forbids
leading zeroes.

Let's report a number with leading zeroes in either part of a score,
or in a score without a total, with its own message that says so.
Leading zeroes are still rejected.

The leading-zero message wins over the size and range messages, e.g.
for 02147483648 or 011/10, because the format is checked before the
values, as before. Input that is wrong in another way as well, e.g.
-05, keeps the general message.

Fixes #136

commitResults.messageTitle: Treat differently encoded equal titles as one
commitResults.messageBody:
A homework title is compared code unit by code unit after its
whitespace is normalized. An accented letter such as é can be typed
as one character (U+00E9) or as e followed by a combining accent
(U+0301). The two look the same, but count as different titles, so a
student can get two homework records that look identical, although
duplicates are rejected.

Let's convert each title to Unicode NFC when it is created. Equal
titles then have the same text, so the duplicate checks of the add
and edit commands and of the data file see them as duplicates, and
the length limit counts the composed characters.

NFC is used instead of NFKC, as NFKC changes characters that look
different, e.g. the superscript in x² becomes a plain 2.

Fixes #137

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject homework titles without visible characters
commitResults.messageBody:
A homework title is rejected only when it is empty after its
whitespace is removed. A zero-width space (U+200B) is not whitespace,
so a title made of it alone is accepted, and the homework appears to
have a blank title in the list and in command results.

Let's remove invisible format characters (Unicode category Cf) and
blank fillers, such as the Hangul filler U+3164, at both ends of a
title, as whitespace is, and reject a title that has no visible
character left, saying in the error message that a title needs one.
A title typed with a zero-width space before it is then the same
title as without it.

Characters inside a title are kept, because some invisible ones are
part of what is shown, e.g. the zero-width joiners that combine
several emoji into one family emoji. For the same reason, the tag
characters that end emoji flags and the variation selector that ends
emoji such as a red heart are never removed, though they do not count
as visible, and format characters that are shown, such as the Arabic
number sign, count as visible.

Fixes #139

commitResults.messageTitle: Use a character allowlist for homework titles
commitResults.messageBody:
A homework title accepts any character except line breaks and control
characters. To keep a title from looking blank, Title trims format
characters and blank fillers from both ends and keeps several lists of
special characters, such as variation selectors, tag characters and
format characters that are shown, to decide what counts as visible.

These lists are hard to read and maintain, and they still accept an
invisible character inside a title. For example, a zero-width space in
"Alge<U+200B>bra drill" makes it a different title from
"Algebra drill", so it passes the duplicate check although the two
look the same. Titles are also the only text field that uses a
denylist; student names use a short allowlist.

Let's use one allowlist rule, like the one for student names: after
NFC and whitespace normalization, a title may contain only letters,
numbers, punctuation, symbols and spaces. Invisible characters are
rejected wherever they are, which fixes the zero-width space inside a
title, and a title of only a zero-width space is still rejected.
Line breaks and tabs from an edited data file become a space, as they
do in names.

An allowlist is chosen over printable ASCII, as accented titles such
as "Café", and data files with them, keep working, and titles are not
stricter than names. As for names, emoji joined by invisible
characters, such as a red heart with U+FE0F, and scripts that use
combining vowel signs, such as Tamil, Hindi or Thai, are rejected.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject trailing content and repeated JSON keys
commitResults.messageBody:
JsonUtil#fromJsonString reads the first JSON value of a file and
ignores the rest. A data file with a second root object after the
first one loads without an error, showing only the first roster, and
the next command that changes the data saves over the file, so the
second object is lost without a warning (Issue #149).

A key repeated in one JSON object, such as a second "students" key,
loses data the same way: Jackson keeps only the last value, so the
students under the first key do not load and the next save deletes
them from the file.

The UG promises that invalid data stops TutorFlow before the roster
opens and leaves the file unchanged.

Let's check that nothing but whitespace follows the JSON value, and
turn on Jackson's STRICT_DUPLICATE_DETECTION, so that both kinds of
file throw an IOException and take the existing invalid-data path:
the error dialog, and no change to the file.

Jackson 2.7, which the project uses, has no FAIL_ON_TRAILING_TOKENS
(added in 2.9), so the check asks the parser for a next token.
Trailing spaces and line breaks, and a leading UTF-8 byte order mark,
still load. Preferences go through the same method, so trailing
content or a repeated key in preferences.json now gives the default
preferences, as for any other invalid preferences file.

commitResults.messageTitle: Print homework indices with ASCII digits
commitResults.messageBody:
`homework list` and `homework upcoming` format their lines with
String.format and the default locale. Under a locale such as ar-EG,
the homework numbers and the `Student N:` numbers come out as
Arabic-Indic digits (`١.`), which the index parsers reject, so the
user cannot type the numbers back into other commands (Issue #151).
The inferred year of `homework add` and `homework edit` has the same
problem, next to a due date that is always in ASCII digits.

Let's format these lines with Locale.ROOT, so the numbers are in the
digits 0 to 9 in every locale.

The parsers keep accepting ASCII digits only, and the default locale
of the app is not changed, so other output is as before. The record
counts in the summary lines are not indices and keep the default
locale.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use default preferences when GUI settings are null
commitResults.messageBody:
Jackson sets the fields of UserPrefs directly, so a preferences.json
holding {"guiSettings":null} loads as UserPrefs with null GUI
settings. ModelManager then copies them through
UserPrefs#setGuiSettings, which rejects null, and TutorFlow stops with
a NullPointerException before any window opens, on every launch until
the user fixes the file by hand (Issue #152).

Let's treat a null guiSettings as invalid preferences: readUserPrefs
throws a DataLoadingException, and MainApp#initPrefs falls back to the
default preferences, as it does for unreadable preferences, and saves
them over the file. The data file is not touched. The fallback warning
now also logs the cause.

A missing guiSettings keeps its default, as before. Other null values
are left as they are because they do not crash: a null
windowCoordinates means no saved position, null window sizes load as
0 and the window's minimum size applies, and unknown keys such as
addressBookFilePath are ignored.

commitResults.messageTitle: Find the end of quoted values in linear time
commitResults.messageBody:
To decide whether a quoted value ends at a quote, the tokenizer checks
whether only whitespace follows that quote by copying the rest of the
arguments and calling isBlank on the copy. It does this for every
candidate quote, so a value made of many quotes takes quadratic time:
`hw up due/` followed by 200,000 quotes blocks the GUI for seconds
before the day-count error appears (Issue #154).

Let's find the end of the non-whitespace text once, and compare each
quote's position with it. stripTrailing and isBlank use the same
definition of whitespace, so the result is the same for every input;
a comparison of the old and new tokenizer on all token sequences up
to length 6 and on random longer inputs found no difference.

The new tests use 1,000,000 quotes, which took over 8 s before this
change on a fast machine and now take milliseconds. Input length is
not capped.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject data files that are not valid UTF-8
commitResults.messageBody:
FileUtil#readFromFile decodes the file with new String(bytes, UTF-8),
which replaces each invalid byte with U+FFFD. A data file saved in
another encoding, such as a title with a Windows-1252 é (byte E9),
loads without an error and shows `R�vision`, and the next command that
changes the data saves U+FFFD over the original bytes, so they cannot
be recovered (Issue #156).

The UG says the data file is UTF-8 and that invalid data stops
TutorFlow before the roster opens, leaving the file unchanged.

Let's decode with a UTF-8 decoder that reports malformed input, and
throw an IOException that gives the offset of the first invalid byte.
Such a file takes the existing invalid-data path: the error dialog,
and no change to the file. Valid UTF-8, with or without a byte order
mark, loads as before.

preferences.json is read the same way, so invalid UTF-8 there gives
the default preferences, as for any other invalid preferences file.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add failing tests for unknown prefix errors
commitResults.messageBody:
An unknown prefix-shaped word (km/ in "t/Speed in km/h", x/y) gives
only the command's generic format message, which the user's input
already matches, and title/ with t/ says "Prefix title/ must be
specified exactly once."

These tests encode the fix agreed in OWN_ISSUES.md B-01: name the
word, add the quoting hint with an example built from the field's
text (no example when the text is only digits and date or time
punctuation, no hint when the word is not inside any value), add a
straight-quote hint for curly quotes, keep the usage line, and say
"Use either title/ or t/, not both." for the title alias clash.

They fail until the fix is implemented.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add failing tests for due date errors and year range
commitResults.messageBody:
Every due-date mistake gets one message, which for due/2-29 names the
very format the user typed, and any year from 0001 to 9999 is
accepted, in commands and in the data file.

These tests encode the fix agreed in OWN_ISSUES.md B-02: separate
messages for an empty date, a wrong format and a date that does not
exist, a 29 February message naming the next leap year, and years
from 2000 to 2099 only (year checked first), with the same three
cases when loading the data file.

They fail until the fix is implemented.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add failing tests for homework delete renumbering
commitResults.messageBody:
After hw del the remaining homework is renumbered, but the result
shows only the deleted record (without its score or status), so a
second delete from the numbers shown before removes the wrong record.

These tests encode the fix agreed in OWN_ISSUES.md B-03: show the
deleted record in the hw ls line layout, then the student's upcoming
homework with the new numbers, using the same text as hw edit.

HomeworkDeleteCommand needs today's date for the upcoming list. The
fix adds it to the constructor, so CommandTestUtil builds the command
reflectively until then and the tests fail on their assertions.

They fail until the fix is implemented.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add failing tests for save failure causes
commitResults.messageBody:
A failed save shows raw system text, or a command message that gives
no reason, and never names the data file.

These tests encode the fix agreed in OWN_ISSUES.md B-05: name the
data file relative to the home folder and give a plain cause (a
folder in place of the file, a read-only file or data folder, or a
file in the way of the data folder), falling back to the system text.

The fix gives LogicManager the home folder and passes the name and
cause to getSaveFailureMessage, so the tests reach both reflectively
until then and fail on their assertions.

They fail until the fix is implemented.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add failing tests for help window row order
commitResults.messageBody:
The help window lists each section's rows in an order that matches
neither the user guide nor the command summary, and the list row does
not show its ls alias.

These tests encode the fix agreed in OWN_ISSUES.md B-06: list every
section in the user guide order and show list|ls in the list row.

They fail until the fix is implemented.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add failing tests for help example and load reason
commitResults.messageBody:
The help window's homework edit example puts an algebra title on the
first sample student's physics record, and the dialog shown when the
data file is rejected gives the same text for every cause.

These tests encode the fix agreed in OWN_ISSUES.md B-07: use
hw e 1 2 t/Kinematics practice set B as the example, and show the
reason from the load exception's cause in the dialog. They also pin
the status rules the user guide will describe (any case, and a
misspelled key loads as ASSIGNED), which already pass.

The date reasons also need the B-02 fix. The tests fail until the
fixes are implemented.

commitResults.messageTitle: Cover hw add with the title alias and no due date
commitResults.messageBody:
The developer guide's manual test runs hw add 1 t/A s/MATH, but no
automated test covers a missing due/ with the t/ alias and a valid
index.

OWN_ISSUES.md B-08 asks for this test while the guide is updated.
It passes today and guards the message the guide will show.

commitResults.messageTitle: Assert exact wrong-format date message for files
commitResults.messageBody:
The data-file tests for a wrongly formatted due date only check that
the message starts with the date and names YYYY-MM-DD, because the
wording was not agreed when they were written.

The agreed wording is now "<date> is not in YYYY-MM-DD format, e.g.
2026-10-30.", recorded in OWN_ISSUES.md (B-02).

Let's assert that exact text in the due date, storage and startup
dialog tests, so the fix for B-02 and B-07 must use it.

commitResults.messageTitle: Say what is wrong with a due date
commitResults.messageBody:
Every due-date mistake gets one message, "Due date must be a valid
calendar date in YYYY-MM-DD or MM-DD format ...", whether the format
is wrong, the date does not exist or due/2-29 is typed in a year
whose next 29 February is more than a year away. For due/2-29 it
tells the user to use the very format they used. Any year from 0001
to 9999 is accepted, so a typo such as due/2206-10-30 is added as
upcoming homework, and when loading the data file every date error
is replaced by one generic message.

Let's give each case its own message: an empty date, a wrong format,
a date that does not exist, a 29 February that names the next leap
year, and a year outside 2000 to 2099. The year is checked before the
calendar. The data file gets the same checks and keeps the message,
so the load dialog can show it later.

The year range is fixed rather than relative to today, so a data file
that loads today keeps loading in later years.

commitResults.messageTitle: Name the unknown word in prefix errors
commitResults.messageBody:
Any lowercase word followed by / is read as a prefix. When it is not
one the command accepts, such as km/ in "t/Speed in km/h", the error
is only "Invalid command format." with the usage, which the user's
command already matches, so the user cannot tell which word is wrong.
Curly quotes pasted from a document, and a quoted value with no space
after its closing quote, fail the same way. Typing title/ with its
alias t/ says "Prefix title/ must be specified exactly once." although
title/ was typed once.

Let's name the word and, when it is inside a value, show how to quote
that value, using the user's own text, e.g. t/"Speed in km/h". The
example is left out when the text before the word is only a date,
time or number, and the quote hint when the word is not inside any
value. Curly quotes get a line asking for straight quotes. The usage
stays on the next line. title/ with t/ gets "Use either title/ or t/,
not both."

The tokenizer is shared, so every command with prefixes gets the new
message, including the student, filter, sort and lesson commands.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show new homework numbers after a delete
commitResults.messageBody:
After hw del, the remaining homework is renumbered, but the result
shows only the deleted record, so a second delete typed from the list
shown before removes the wrong record, which cannot be undone. The
deleted record is also shown without its score and status.

Let's show the deleted record in the hw ls layout, with the number it
had, its score and its status, followed by the student's upcoming
homework with the new numbers, reusing the list that hw edit already
shows. The command now takes today's date from the parser's clock to
build that list.

The tests that build the command are updated to pass today's date, and
the reflective helper that stood in for the new constructor is
replaced by direct calls.

commitResults.messageTitle: Say why saving failed and name the data file
commitResults.messageBody:
When a command's changes cannot be saved, they are undone, but the
message is raw system text ("Could not save data due to the following
error: Is a directory"), names the internal tutorflow.json.lock file
with an absolute path, or, for the homework, lesson and student edit
commands, gives no reason at all. The user cannot tell what to fix.

Let's work out the likely cause from the file system: the data file
is a folder, the data file is read-only, the data folder is read-only,
or a file is where the data folder should be, in that order, falling
back to the system's text. Name the data file as the user knows it,
relative to the home folder, e.g. data/tutorflow.json. The general
message becomes "Could not save data/tutorflow.json: <cause>. Nothing
was changed.", and each command's own message keeps its wording and
gains the file name and cause.

The cause is read from the file system rather than the exception, as
the exception may be about the lock file or have system-specific
text. A data-file conflict keeps its own message.

The tests now call the new LogicManager constructor and the two-part
save-failure method directly instead of through reflection.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show why the data file was rejected
commitResults.messageBody:
When the data file cannot be loaded, the startup dialog gives the
file's path and recovery steps, but not what is wrong. The reason is
only in the log file, so the user cannot tell which record to fix.

The user guide also has examples that do not match what the app does:
the upcoming homework examples only work on 2026-10-17, the edit
example puts an algebra title on a physics record, the advice for
moving to another computer relies on a data file that a new install
does not have yet, and the data file rules leave out `status` and
one-digit months and days.

Let's
* add a "Reason:" line to the dialog, taken from the load error's
  cause so that it holds no exception class name
* replace Jackson's technical text for a file that is not valid JSON
  with the line and column near the problem; Jackson's column is
  wrong at the end of the input, so work it out from the offset
* use "hw e 1 2 t/Kinematics practice set B" as the edit example in
  the guide and the help window
* give the date-dependent examples with the date they were taken on,
  and fix the FAQ and the data file rules

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix homework gaps in the developer guide
commitResults.messageBody:
The developer guide leaves homework out in several places. The scope,
value proposition and non-functional requirements cover only students
and lessons, all homework user stories are low priority, the homework
section has no diagram, and the prefix splitting section misses
`edit`, `sort` and `lesson edit`. Several manual tests also give
outputs that the app does not show, e.g. `hw up due/365` shows the
same records as `hw up due/0` with the given setup, and `homework
list 1` hides the overdue record that a later step needs.

Let's
* add homework to the scope, the value proposition and NFRs 5, 7, 8
  and 9; the NFR 7 limit of 50 homework records per student was
  measured in the JAR with 100 students, 5000 homework records and
  1000 lessons (each command under 30 ms, excluding the GUI)
* raise the implemented homework stories, and add stories for
  upcoming homework and the help window
* add a class diagram of how a student holds its homework
* list every caller of the prefix splitter
* add a manual test for `homework add`, and fix the manual tests for
  listing, upcoming, deleting, lesson editing and old scores with the
  outputs of the JAR

commitResults.messageTitle: Expect the ls alias only in the help list row
commitResults.messageBody:
One help window test expects every row to show its command's usage
text, so it expects the `list` row to show "Usage: list". Another
test expects that row to show "list|ls".

The agreed fix adds the alias to the help row only and leaves the
usage text of the list command unchanged, as PR #143 changes that
text (Issue #124).

Let's expect "list|ls" for the list row in the usage test as well.
This test fails until the help rows are fixed in the next commit.

commitResults.messageTitle: List help rows in user guide order with ls
commitResults.messageBody:
The help window lists the rows of each section in an order that
matches neither the user guide nor the command summary, as newer
commands were added at the top of their sections. The `list` row
also leaves out the `ls` alias, while the homework list row shows
its alias.

Let's order every section as the user guide does, and show the
`list` row's format as "list|ls". The usage text of the list command
stays unchanged, as PR #143 changes it.

commitResults.messageTitle: Fill in save-failure messages in one place
commitResults.messageBody:
Each of the nine commands with its own save-failure message overrides
the method that builds it, and all nine fill in the data file's name
and the cause with the same code. A new command could fill them in a
different order by mistake.

Let's have each command give only its message format, and let the
base command fill in the name and cause for all of them. Also move
the search for the nearest existing folder on the data file's path
into its own method, so the method that picks the cause reads as a
list of checks.

commitResults.messageTitle: Split the unknown prefix error into steps
commitResults.messageBody:
The method that builds the error for an unknown prefix works out the
quote hint and its example, looks for curly quotes and cuts out the
usage text, all in one body. The two loops that strip quotes from the
example repeat the same condition.

Let's give the quote hint, the curly quote check and the usage text
a method each, so the builder reads as the order of the lines in the
message, and name the repeated condition. The messages stay the same.

commitResults.messageTitle: Name the due date year limits
commitResults.messageBody:
The due date's year range, 2000 to 2099, appears as two private
numbers and again as literal text in the error message, so changing
the range in one place would leave the message wrong.

Let's make the limits named public constants and build the message
from them.

commitResults.messageTitle: Name the data file from the app's home folder
commitResults.messageBody:
A save-failure message names the data file relative to the working
folder, not to the folder that holds the JAR. So when TutorFlow is
started from another folder, e.g. `java -jar app/tutorflow.jar`, the
message says `app/data/tutorflow.json`, and when it is started from
`/`, the path loses its leading slash.

Let's give the app's home folder, which the data file is in, to the
logic component when the app starts, so the message always says
`data/tutorflow.json`.

commitResults.messageTitle: Report a read-only home folder when saving
commitResults.messageBody:
Before the first save, the app's home folder may have no data folder
yet. If the home folder is read-only, the data folder cannot be
created, and the save error shows only the raw system path, e.g.
"Could not save data/tutorflow.json: /Users/.../app/data. Nothing was
changed."

The user is not told which folder to make writable.

Let's look for a read-only folder at the nearest folder on the data
file's path that exists, not only at the data folder. The cause names
that folder as the user knows it: "the data folder is read-only" as
before, "the home folder is read-only", or "the folder store is
read-only" for any other folder, relative to the home folder.

commitResults.messageTitle: Say when the data file is empty
commitResults.messageBody:
An empty data file, or one with only whitespace, cannot be loaded. The
error shows Jackson's text: "No content to map due to end-of-input" and
a source line that holds the file's whitespace.

This tells the user neither what is wrong nor where.

Let's check for a blank file before reading the JSON and give the plain
reason "The file is empty." instead.

commitResults.messageTitle: Tell wrong value types apart from bad JSON
commitResults.messageBody:
A data file that is valid JSON but has a value of the wrong type, e.g.
{"students": 5} or a list where a name is expected, is reported as
"The file is not valid JSON near line L, column C."

The user may look for a syntax error that is not there.

Let's keep that reason only for syntax errors, including those Jackson
finds while mapping a value, and report any other mapping error as
"The file has a value of the wrong type near line L, column C."

commitResults.messageTitle: Point at the character that breaks the JSON
commitResults.messageBody:
The reason for a data file that is not valid JSON gives a line and
column that can be off. For an error found inside a student, such as
"name" : "A",, it points at "A", the start of the value Jackson was
reading, not the second comma. For other syntax errors, it points just
after the character that breaks the JSON.

The user may look in the wrong place for the mistake.

Let's take the position from the syntax error itself, not the error
that wraps it, and move it back onto the character that breaks the
JSON.

commitResults.messageTitle: Print the leap day example in ASCII digits
commitResults.messageBody:
When 29 February is not in the next 12 months, the due date error
gives the next leap day as an example. The year is formatted with the
default locale, so under e.g. ar-EG it reads "e.g. ٢٠٢٨-02-29", and
typing that example back in is rejected as the wrong format.

Let's format the year with Locale.ROOT, as the homework list already
does for its indices, so the example can be typed back in any locale.

commitResults.messageTitle: Give load error positions in ASCII digits
commitResults.messageBody:
The reason for a data file that is not valid JSON, or has a value of
the wrong type, gives a line and column. They are formatted with the
default locale, so under e.g. ar-EG the reason reads "near line ٢,
column ١٨", which does not match the line numbers in a text editor.

Let's format them with Locale.ROOT, as the leap day example is.

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep the due date year limits private
commitResults.messageBody:
The earliest and latest due date years are public, but only the due
date class uses them. Other code uses the year message instead.

Let's make them private, so the range can change in one class without
other code depending on it.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test the reason for data missing its last brace
commitResults.messageBody:
The developer guide's manual test removes the final } from the sample
data and expects the reason to point at line 120, column 5, the last
character that is not whitespace. Only a one-line file that ends too
early is tested, so a long file, where Jackson's own column is far off
(column 3221), is checked only by hand.

Let's add the exact file from that manual test as test data, and check
its reason.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test that dates in Arabic-Indic digits are rejected
commitResults.messageBody:
Under ar-EG, the leap day example was printed as ٢٠٢٨-02-29, and typing
it back in is rejected as the wrong format. Due dates accept only the
digits 0 to 9, but no test gives a date in other digits.

Let's check that exact date in both the command and the data file
forms, so a change to the date patterns cannot start accepting other
digits unnoticed.

commitResults.messageTitle: DG: Cut low-level detail from homework and saving
commitResults.messageBody:
The Storage, homework and saving sections of the developer guide give
library internals and every edge case: Jackson versions and error
offsets, POSIX permissions, Unicode code points, locale digits, every
due-date message constant and the order of the save-failure checks.
UC04 repeats the first steps of UC03, and two manual tests need the app
restarted under an Arabic Java locale.

The Week 10 tutorial lists "not sufficiently high-level", "too long",
"unfamiliar terms" and "unnecessary repetitions" among the DG bugs, and
each extra low-level sentence is one more that can go out of date.

Let's
* condense those paragraphs to what a new developer needs, keeping the
  rationale and design considerations
* let UC04 refer to UC03 for the shared steps and renumber its
  extensions
* drop the two locale manual tests

All other text, the diagrams and the remaining manual tests are
unchanged; their commands were rerun and give the stated output.

Fixes #163

commitResults.messageTitle: DG: Draw a student's homework as an association
commitResults.messageBody:
The homework class diagram draws the link from Student to Homework as
a composition, while the Model class diagram draws the same link as a
plain association. Two diagrams of the same classes disagree.

Composition also overstates the link: Homework objects are immutable
and are shared by the old and the new Student after every change.

Let's draw it as a navigable association, as the Model diagram does.

commitResults.messageTitle: DG: Add diagrams for homework and loading data
commitResults.messageBody:
The homework section explains adding, homework indices and recording
marks in prose only, and the Storage section describes the startup
load in prose only. A new developer has to rebuild each flow in their
head from long paragraphs.

Let's add one diagram for each, with a short lead-in:

* an activity diagram with swimlanes for the checks of homework add
* an object diagram of the homework indices before and after a delete
* a sequence diagram for recording marks, with parsing and saving as
  reference frames so it shows only the Logic details
* an activity diagram for loading the data file at startup

Together with the existing class, sequence and activity diagrams, the
section now uses four kinds of UML diagram.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge pull request #143 from Edison-choo/fix-student-alpha-bugs
commitResults.messageBody:
Fix student alpha testing issues and document student flows

Fix the student add, edit, search and delete bugs found in alpha
testing, so that tutors' typos are caught and valid input is kept.
* edit saves a new subject order instead of reporting no changes
* add and edit reject mistyped prefixes such as ph/ instead of saving
  them inside a name, while keeping relationship words such as s/o,
  d/o, a/l, a/p and w/o
* edit and add treat a phone with and without +65 as the same student,
  and a duplicate edit names the existing student
* search ignores case for every letter and collapses repeated spaces
* edit and delete say why a save failed
* the roster shows the full guardian name in a tooltip
The help window, User Guide and Developer Guide match these rules, and
the Developer Guide completes the student use cases and delete steps.

commitResults.messageTitle: DG: Move lesson sections after homework sections
commitResults.messageBody:
In the Implementation section, the two regular-lesson sections sit
between "Homework management" and the other homework sections
("Filtering homework", "Updating homework completion").

Sections on the same feature should be next to each other, so that a
reader finds all homework design in one place.

Let's move "Adding regular lessons" and "Editing regular lessons" to
just before "Saving after a command".

This commit only moves lines: the sorted lines of the old and new
DeveloperGuide.md are identical.

commitResults.messageTitle: DG: Give each homework feature its own section
commitResults.messageBody:
"Homework management" is one section that mixes parsing, storage,
adding, listing, upcoming homework, deleting, editing and marks. A
reader cannot find the design of one homework feature from the table
of contents.

Let's split it into "Homework records" (parsing, storage, the homework
index and the design considerations shared by every homework command),
"Adding homework", "Listing a student's homework", "Listing upcoming
homework", "Deleting homework" and "Editing homework and recording
marks".

The existing paragraphs and diagrams move into these sections with
their wording kept; only bold run-in labels that repeat the new
headings are dropped. "homework list" and "homework upcoming" are
explained in prose only, so let's add an activity diagram of which
records "homework list" shows and a sequence diagram of "homework
upcoming" reading the whole roster and resetting the displayed list.
"homework edit" gets a short paragraph, as it has no description yet.

commitResults.messageTitle: DG: Make the homework diagrams easier to read
commitResults.messageBody:
The homework class diagram repeats the Homework part of the Model
class diagram and does not show how homework is changed. The add
activity diagram is tall, as its four swimlanes push each step down
and across. The marks and upcoming sequence diagrams start with a
ref frame such as "parse ... into c", which readers do not
understand, and use one-letter object names.

Let's show the homework fields as attributes, with the methods that
change homework and a note that both classes are immutable; draw the
add checks in one flow with each failure beside its check, about
half the old height; and replace the parse ref frames with a plain
note and the one-letter names with readable ones.

commitResults.messageTitle: DG: Explain the homework features in plain words
commitResults.messageBody:
The homework and saving sections use long sentences and few
examples, so a new developer has to read some rules several times,
e.g. why a second delete can remove the wrong record.

Let's shorten the sentences and add one small example from the
sample data where it makes a rule obvious: duplicate homework,
homework indices in hw ls, upcoming homework, a second delete and an
unchanged edit. Every example was run against the code. The save
failure step now also lists DeleteCommand, which has its own save
failure message.

commitResults.messageTitle: UG: Group commands by feature
commitResults.messageBody:
The Features section lists `delete` and `clear` among the homework
commands, and `exit` between the homework and lesson commands. The
command summary mixes the student, homework and lesson rows the same
way.

A reader looking for every student command has to search the whole
section.

Let's order the sections as students, homework, lessons, then `exit`,
followed by the data-file sections, and order the command summary rows
the same way.

This commit only moves whole sections and table rows: the sorted lines
of the old and new file are identical.

commitResults.messageTitle: Say how many earlier homework records are hidden
commitResults.messageBody:
Without `all`, homework list leaves out homework due before today but
keeps the other records' numbers, so the list can start at 2 or have
gaps. The summary line does not say that anything was left out. After
`hw e 2 1 t/Research Organic pathways` on the sample data, Priya Nair's
list starts at 2, and users take the gap for a numbering bug.

Let's have the summary line say how many records due before today are
not shown and which command lists them, e.g. "Listed 2 upcoming
homework records for Priya Nair (1 record due before today not shown;
use homework list 2 all to see it)." The "No upcoming homework found"
message gets the same note. The line is unchanged when nothing is
hidden and with `all`.

The note says "due before today", the words the user guide uses for
what the list leaves out, rather than "overdue": it also counts
completed homework, while the student card's "Overdue homework" counts
only ASSIGNED homework.

homework edit and homework delete show the same list, so they pass the
STUDENT_INDEX the user typed, which is the index the hinted command
needs. The index is printed with Locale.ROOT so that it can be typed
back in every locale.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test when the hidden homework note changes
commitResults.messageBody:
The note about homework left out of the list is tested for homework
list and for the typed STUDENT_INDEX after a search, but not for the
cases alpha testing tried by hand: deleting the only record due before
today, editing a due date out of the past, and editing or deleting
after `filter` or `sort` has moved the student away from their roster
position.

Let's add command tests for each of these and LogicManager tests with
the commands from the alpha test on the sample students, run on
2026-10-28:

* `hw del 2 1` and `hw e 2 1 due/2026-12-01` drop the note.
* `filter s/CHEMISTRY` then `hw e 1 2 t/Pathways map v2`, and
  `sort by/level o/desc` then `hw del 4 2`, name the displayed index,
  and the named command lists the hidden record.

The code already behaves this way, so only tests change. Passing the
roster position instead of the typed index fails the four new filter
and sort tests and no other test.

commitResults.messageTitle: Docs: Show the hidden homework note in list docs
commitResults.messageBody:
The homework list activity diagram has no step for the note about
records due before today left out, although the developer guide text
above it describes the note. The user guide says the result starts
with `Listed N upcoming homework records for NAME.`, which reads as
the exact first line, but with the note the period comes after it.

Let's add a "some records left out" step that adds the note before
the result is shown, and say the result starts with a line "such as"
that one.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge pull request #178 from wyekstudent/branch-170-student-day-filter
commitResults.messageBody:
Support student filtering by regular meeting day

Add an optional d/DAY criterion to filter, so tutors can list the
students who have a regular lesson on a given weekday. A day matches
any of the student's lessons on that weekday, and is combined with the
level and subject criteria using AND; the subject is checked against
the student's registration, not the lesson's subject.

The day uses the same full-weekday rules as the lesson commands. The
active filter description shows the day, and lesson changes update
which students match while the criteria stay in place. Filtering
still never saves, and student indices follow the displayed list.

The history is kept in memory only and is never saved. It includes

commitResults.messageTitle: Preserve typed FXML loading failures

student view from recovering without also catching programming errors.

cause. This gives the rendering boundary a recoverable exception while
leaving genuine assertion failures visible.

Update loader expectations and validate all UI tests and Checkstyle.

commitResults.messageTitle: Handle recoverable student card rendering failures
commitResults.messageBody:
JavaFX can render student cells after command execution, outside the
command's exception handler.

Handle recoverable cell failures at the student panel boundary. Clear
the failed graphic, log the technical cause once per rendering attempt
and notify the owner without changing student records.

Keep assertion failures visible. Add an injectable card factory and
focused JavaFX tests for recovery and diagnostic logging.

Validate the panel and existing student UI tests with Checkstyle.

commitResults.messageTitle: Report filter rendering failures in the UI
commitResults.messageBody:
Rendering can fail during a roster update or later when JavaFX creates
a cell. Command success feedback must not hide either failure.

Connect the panel's recovery callback to the result display and retain
its error message when rendering fails during command execution.
Allow a later command to begin a fresh rendering attempt.

selection and viewport preservation, deferred failures and recovery.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document student filtering and help

commitResults.messageTitle: Add stable student sorting rules

meeting day without changing student records or dropping occurrences.

last in either direction and use the same minimum value in both orders.

commitResults.messageTitle: Separate displayed student order from roster order
commitResults.messageBody:
A filtered view follows stored order and cannot retain an independent
student sort. Reordering the stored roster would also trigger a save.

occurrences and follows replacement, removal and insertion changes.

failures for recovery and refresh card indices when cells move.

Related to #78

commitResults.messageTitle: Recover student sorts at the UI boundary
commitResults.messageBody:
A completed model sort can still fail while JavaFX renders its cards.
Reporting success before checking that rendering leaves the displayed
order and selection inconsistent with the reported command outcome.

Verify sort rendering before reporting success. Restore the prior order
and view on failure, preserve retry input and log the technical cause
once at WARNING after recovery or SEVERE if restoration also fails.
